crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: The AI Enablement Audit in Finance
children.blurb: An AI enablement audit in finance examines whether an organization's use of AI systems is fit for purpose, properly documented, and aligned with internal controls and external obligations.

children.name: Keeping Financial Data Out of Public Models
children.blurb: Keeping financial data out of public models means preventing account numbers, transaction details, client portfolios, earnings figures, and other sensitive records from being absorbed into models whose weights, outputs, or training sets are publicly accessible.

children.name: Model Risk and Bias Testing
children.blurb: Model risk and bias testing covers the formal review of quantitative models used in lending, pricing, fraud detection, capital allocation, and other financial decisions.

children.name: Mapping Financial AI to the Rules
children.blurb: This page maps where financial AI systems intersect with formal rules, including prudential regulation, securities law, anti-money laundering requirements, data protection, and contractual obligations.

children.name: Local and Air-Gapped Deployment
children.blurb: Local and air-gapped deployment means running AI models and supporting systems entirely on an organization's own hardware and network, with no connection to external cloud services or the public internet.

sections.body: This field covers the practical controls around using artificial intelligence in financial work. It includes checking whether an AI system is actually ready for a finance team, stopping sensitive data from leaking into shared models, testing models for bias and failure, matching AI use to regulations, and running systems on local or isolated hardware. The site tracks 210 compliance and regulation pages and 142 active AI lawsuits, which shows how much legal and supervisory attention this area receives. The work is not about debating whether AI should exist in finance, it is about auditing, containing, and documenting what is already being used.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts of this field are more settled than others. Data leakage controls and local deployment are well understood, with clear technical options for keeping financial records out of public models. Model risk and bias testing is active but far from solved, because financial models can fail in ways that only appear under stress or across different customer groups. Regulatory mapping is fragmented, since rules differ by jurisdiction and many AI-specific requirements are still being written. The honest limit is that no audit or test can guarantee a model will behave correctly in every future market condition. The site's 352 merger and acquisition filings and 117 listed AI-related instruments suggest that the financial products and corporate structures around AI are changing faster than the rulebooks.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader should start with The AI Enablement Audit in Finance to see how a finance team evaluates whether an AI tool is worth deploying at all. Keeping Financial Data Out of Public Models then explains the specific technical and policy controls for preventing leakage. Model Risk and Bias Testing goes deeper into the statistical and operational checks that follow deployment. Mapping Financial AI to the Rules connects those checks to the 210 compliance and regulation pages tracked on this site. Local and Air-Gapped Deployment covers the infrastructure choices for organizations that cannot send data offsite, which often becomes the final requirement after the other pages identify a risk. Together they move from initial approval to containment, testing, legal alignment, and physical isolation.
